sources.entry: Buttercup Desktop - Secure password manager for mac and other platforms.

summary.one_liner: Buttercup Desktop is a free, open-source, cross-platform password manager app for Mac, Linux and Windows that stores encrypted vaults in .bcup files.
summary.what_it_does: Buttercup encrypts passwords and other credentials into protected .bcup vault files using industry-standard encryption. Vaults can be loaded from and saved to the local filesystem, Dropbox, Google Drive, or any WebDAV-enabled service such as ownCloud or Nextcloud. The desktop app is built on Electron, Node.js and TypeScript. It offers an offline vault cache, command-line flags for autostart, hidden launch and disabling update checks, and a portable Windows build configurable through environment variables. The README also describes config, vault storage, cache and log file locations for each OS. The project has been closed and is in transition to a public archive, and the README asks users not to open issues or PRs.
use_cases: sync a password vault via Dropbox or Google Drive
keep a password vault on Nextcloud or ownCloud via WebDAV
run a portable password manager from a USB drive on Windows
generate unique strong passwords for online accounts
how_to_run: Download the appropriate installer or AppImage from the Buttercup Desktop releases page
For development: ensure Node v16 or greater and NPM v7 or greater are installed
In one terminal run `npm run start:build`
In a second terminal run `npm run start:main`
notable: Vaults can be stored on local disk, Dropbox, Google Drive or any WebDAV service
Portable Windows build configurable with BUTTERCUP_HOME_DIR, BUTTERCUP_CONFIG_DIR and BUTTERCUP_TEMP_DIR
Linux distributed as an AppImage that supports auto-updating
Vault files use the .bcup format with encryption at rest
caveats: Project is closed; the README says it is moving to a public archive and issues and PRs will be ignored
Only x64 builds are supported; Apple Silicon builds are not yet available and 32-bit builds were dropped
Version 1 is no longer maintained; Google Drive auth on Linux requires AppImageLauncher
